--- title: "Vision II: The retina" format: revealjs --- # Preliminaries ## Announcement - Quiz 3 this Friday. ## Today's topics - Warm-up - The retina # Warm-up --- ### The image of visual patterns projecting onto the retina is: - A. Inside out and rotated. - B. Upside down and left/right reversed. - C. Unrecognizably distorted by the cornea and lens. - D. Larger in one eye than the other. --- ### The image of visual patterns projecting onto the retina is: - A. ~~Inside out and rotated.~~ - B. **Upside down and left/right reversed.** - C. ~~Unrecognizably distorted by the cornea and lens.~~ - D. ~~Larger in one eye than the other.~~ --- ### Visual information allows the perceiver to extract information about all of the following properties, EXCEPT: - A. Object position (where is it?) - B. Object density (mass/volume) - C. Object type/identity (what is it?) - D. Time (of day/year) --- ### Visual information allows the perceiver to extract information about all of the following properties, EXCEPT: - A. Object position (where is it?) - B. **Object density (mass/volume)** - C. Object type/identity (what is it?) - D. Time (of day/year) # The retina --- ![Retinal rods (green) & cones (blue)](https://i.pinimg.com/originals/9f/08/85/9f0885d4c209d5275f631ac194eb4f4b.jpg){#fig-rods-cones} ## How photoreceptors work :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width=50%} - Outer segment + Membrane disks + *Photopigments* - Sense light, trigger chemical cascade ::: ::: {.column width=50%} ![@Land1999-af](https://cdn.britannica.com/44/55744-050-4F61301B/cells-cones-eye-retina-segment-rod-phototransduction.jpg) ::: :::: ## How photoreceptors work :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width=50%} - Inner segment + Synaptic terminal - Light *hyperpolarizes* photoreceptor! + The *dark current* - *Less* light $\rightarrow$ more NT (glutamate)! ::: ::: {.column width=50%} ![@Land1999-af](https://cdn.britannica.com/44/55744-050-4F61301B/cells-cones-eye-retina-segment-rod-phototransduction.jpg) ::: :::: ## Retina - Physiologically *backwards* + How? - Anatomically *inside-out* + How? ## Retina - Physiologically *backwards* + Dark current (more NT released in dark than light) - Anatomically *inside-out* + Photoreceptors at back of eye --- ### Photoreceptors are arranged in mosaics ![Normal color vision vs. protanopic (color blind) vision; Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinal_mosaic](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a6/ConeMosaics.jpg){#fig-cone-rod-mosaics} --- ### with different concentrations in different parts of the retina ![https://book.bionumbers.org/how-big-is-a-photoreceptor/](https://book.bionumbers.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/130-f2-RodCellDensity-12.png){#fig-book-bionumbers} ## Photoreceptor distribution - Retinal periphery - Mostly rods - Retinal center/fovea - Mostly cones - ~1-2 deg of visual angle --- ![@UnknownUnknown-qs](https://nightsky.jpl.nasa.gov/media/images/Handy_Degrees_NSN_8961.original.jpg){#fig-visual-field-approx width="65%"} ## Consequences - Must move eyes (or eyes/head or eyes/head/body) to position fovea on target - Keep track of sequence of eye movements and positions over time - Integrate sequence of samples over time --- ![@Cairo2013-hm Figure 5.6](../include/img/cairo-fig-5.6.png) ## Retinal information processing :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width=50%} - Separate channels for - Achromatic (black/gray/white) info - Mostly rods - Chromatic - Mostly cones - Short, medium, long wavelength types ::: ::: {.column width=50%} - Pixels/photoreceptor analogy - ~120 M rods + ~ 5 M cones (125 M) - vs. professional cameras with 100 M pixels ::: :::: ## Retinal information processing - Point by point, topographic (map-like) 2D image of 3D world - Non-uniform resolution (center >> periphery) - yields focused image except... --- ### ...when eye misshapen for cornea+lens ![https://heffingtons.com/myopia-vs-hyperopia/](../include/img/myopia-hyperopia.jpg){#fig-myopia-hyperopia width="65%"} ## Color perception :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width=50%} - Perceived color a function of activity in "R", "G", and "B" photoreceptors ::: ::: {.column width=50%} ![http://hyperphysics.phy-astr.gsu.edu/hbase/vision/colcon.html](http://hyperphysics.phy-astr.gsu.edu/hbase/vision/imgvis/colcon.png){#fig-color-perception} ::: :::: ## Wavelengths are continuous, but are perceived colors? ![https://rmit.pressbooks.pub/colourtheory1/part/2-colour-theory-the-visible-spectrum/](https://rmit.pressbooks.pub/app/uploads/sites/42/2022/10/visitble-spectrum-nm.png) ## Color vision anomalies :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width=50%} - Absence of or anomalies in photoreceptors ::: ::: {.column width=50%} ![https://bluefinvision.com/ishihara-colour-blind-test-online/](https://bluefinvision.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/eye-tests-ishihara-colour-blind-test.webp){#fig-ishihara width="55%"} ::: :::: ## Types :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width=40%} - Protanopia (impaired R/long wavelength) - Deuteranopia (impaired G/medium wavelength) - Tritanopia (impaired B/short wavelength) ::: ::: {.column width=60%} ![https://www.color-blindness.com/protanopia-red-green-color-blindness/](https://www.color-blindness.com/wp-content/images/Protanopia-Color-Spectrum.jpg){#fig-color-vision-anomolies} ::: :::: # From retina to brain
## From eye to brain - Retinal ganglion cells - 1st cells with long axons - 1st to generate action potentials - 2nd/II cranial (optic) nerve + Optic chiasm ## From eye to brain - Hypothalamus + Suprachiasmatic nucleus - Regulates circadian (day/night) rhythm via pineal gland --- ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinohypothalamic_tract](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/55/Circadian_rhythm_labeled.jpg){fig-align='center' width=700px} ::: ::: ## From eye to brain - Superior colliculus & brainstem ## *Lateral Geniculate Nucleus (LGN)* of thalamus - ~90% of axons from retina
## LGN - 6 layers + intralaminar zone + Parvocellular (small cells): chromatic + Magnocellular (big cells): achromatic + Koniocellular (chromatic - short wavelength?) - Retinotopic map of opposite visual field ## From LGN to V1
## From LGN to V1 - Via optic radiations - *[Primary visual cortex (V1)](http://www.scholarpedia.org/article/Area_V1)* in occipital lobe ## References {.smaller}

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
